title: Liverpool announce ticket price increases for next three seasons
content:
Liverpool have announced that they will increase ticket prices at Anfield by three per cent next season.

There will also be inflation-linked rises for supporters in the following two campaigns.

Owner Fenway Sports Group (FSG) had frozen prices across the board in eight of the previous 10 years and this will be the first time since they bought the club in 2010 that the price of seats in the iconic Kop stand have increased.

It means that adult general admission tickets, which currently cost between £39 and £61, will rise between £1.25 and £1.75 per game for the 2026-27 season. Adult season tickets, which currently cost between £713 and £904, will increase between £21.50 and £27 next term – up to £1.42 more per game.

The Supporters’ Board said on Thursday they were “extremely disappointed” with such a move “during times of global uncertainty”.

“We’ve engaged with the club in direct discussions since early February,” the statement read. “This followed a meeting with the club’s board and ownership last October. We were clear about our requests throughout: we sought a price freeze for two seasons, in line with the FSA’s ‘Stop Exploiting Loyalty’ campaign, and sought commitment to work together to find alternatives that do not cost supporters more.

“We felt this was an opportunity for the club to do what we might expect from those who pride themselves on it meaning ‘more’: be different from others, support fan loyalty, and work collectively on a solution that does not come at the expense of supporters.

“We wanted to see LFC lead the way. Sadly, they have chosen a path that leads the way in the wrong direction.”

Price changes for the next three seasons will be in line with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) annual inflation rate from January of that year up to a maximum increase of five per cent per season. The CPI monitors the price of goods and services consumed by UK households. The rate in January 2026 was up three per cent.

The decision follows extensive discussions with the club’s Supporters’ Board, who had been pushing for a price freeze for the next two seasons in line with the Football Supporters’ Association campaign against ticket price increases.

The club decided this was not viable due to rising costs beyond their control. They argued that matchday operating costs at Anfield have increased by 85 per cent since 2016-17 and that in the past four years, utility costs have gone up 107 per cent, business rates by 286 per cent and wages, excluding player salaries, by 73 per cent.

Junior tickets and local general tickets (available to fans with a Liverpool post code) will remain frozen at £9 and the upper age for young adult tickets will rise from 21 to 24 from next season, increasing the number of supporters eligible for a 50 per cent discount on adult general admission tickets.

The senior concessions age range remains unchanged, despite the club considering whether to increase the upper age limit in line with the state pension age.
